intent: I kept the wheel track at 0.18 to maintain the improved lateral stability observed in the last iteration, which helps reduce off-track failures. I moved the two rear sensors slightly further back from y = -0.03 to y = -0.035 to enable even earlier detection of sharp turns, giving the controller more time to react and potentially reduce line loss events. I kept the sensor size at 0.016 to preserve noise robustness. These changes aim to provide the controller with better early line information and a stable platform, improving completion rates and progress while reducing line loss events and off-track terminations.
rationale: The previous iteration increased wheel track to 0.18 and moved rear sensors to y = -0.03, which improved stability and early turn detection but the robot still failed early with one line loss event per run and off-track termination around 10% progress. The integrator feedback suggests moving rear sensors further back to y = -0.035 to detect turns even earlier, which should help the controller respond more aggressively to early line deviations. Maintaining the wheel track at 0.18 preserves lateral stability. Sensor size remains at 0.016 for noise robustness. I expect these geometry changes to reduce line loss events, improve progress and completion rates, and provide a more stable and responsive platform for the controller to exploit. I request measurements of completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, and line_loss_events to verify these hypotheses in the next race.
